first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. James wants to talk about the ring properly before we lock anything in, and every lab-grown page I've opened tonight is a jeweller with a 'shop now' button. This one opens by saying it sells neither, so I kept going. I skimmed the takeaways, read the short answer, the GIA report changes, the 'worth it if' list and the paperwork bit properly, and skipped most of the HPHT temperatures and the FTC detail.

journey.quote: Lab grown diamonds have moved from curiosity to the centre of the engagement ring conversation, and almost everything written about them comes from someone selling one side.
journey.reaction: Yes. That's exactly my problem with everything else I've read. Saying it up front makes me trust the rest.

journey.quote: If you can comfortably choose either stone, the question is not whether you can afford natural.
journey.reaction: Finally someone who doesn't assume lab-grown is the budget option. That's our situation, and it's not tacky to say so.

journey.quote: Since 1 October 2025, GIA describes colourless lab-grown diamonds as "Premium" or "Standard" rather than on the colour and clarity scales it uses for natural stones.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that, and it explains why two quotes I was sent didn't line up. Insider-level detail, the kind I actually want.

journey.quote: A capsule holding a carbon source and a mix of metals is heated to about 1300 to 1600°C at pressures of 5 to 6 GPa, the equivalent of 150 to 190 km beneath the Earth's surface.
journey.reaction: Interesting for about two seconds, then I scrolled. I don't need the physics to decide.

journey.quote: Here is how they compare, without prices.
journey.reaction: I get why, but 'reduced price point' tells me nothing. Is it half? A fifth? Even a rough range or 'ask for both quotes on the same spec' would help me plan.

journey.quote: For a proposal abroad, carry the report and receipt.
journey.reaction: Good, practical, and the first hint these people think about travel. I'd have liked one more line on what else to sort before flying with a ring.

journey.quote: These are US rules, as at October 2026, but they are the clearest naming benchmark the industry has.
journey.reaction: Honest that it's American, but this whole section is long for us in Sydney. I'd skim it again.

journey.quote: You may hear firm opinions on both sides, from jewellers and from family.
journey.reaction: Ha. James's mum has already said something. Nice that it's acknowledged without taking sides. I'd send this section to her.

journey.quote: You want the look and the size you love, and would rather put the difference towards the proposal, the honeymoon or the wedding itself.
journey.reaction: This is the actual conversation we're having. Honest trade-off, both columns feel fair.

journey.quote: Any treatment, buy-back or upgrade terms in writing before you pay.
journey.reaction: Clear checklist I can screenshot and take into the jeweller. Exactly how I like advice.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready, your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your one point of contact, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing first is reassuring. 'One point of contact' is what every planner says, though. On a ring page I'm not going to enquire off this alone.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much less is lab-grown for a comparable stone? Even a range or a 'how to compare quotes like for like' tip would help.
If we propose overseas, is there anything beyond the report and receipt to sort (insurance, travelling with the ring)?
Does a Wedded Advisor help with anything ring-related, or is that purely the jeweller's job?
Is there any Australian lab or Australian-specific paperwork we should know about, given most of the rules quoted are US?
would_share_with: James (the 'worth it if, think twice if' section)

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: It's low-pressure and ties to a proposal abroad, which is a nice bridge. But we haven't picked a destination and I came here about a ring, so I'd more likely click through to the destinations page first and enquire after reading a couple more posts and a real wedding.

top_3_changes: Give some sense of the price gap (a range, or how to compare two quotes on the same spec), since 'reduced price point' alone reads like vague pricing.
Trim the FTC and HPHT/CVD detail for Australian readers; the plain-English checklists are where the page is strongest.
Expand the proposal-abroad line slightly (what to sort before travelling with a ring) so the bridge to the destination CTA feels earned.

checks.check: Every journey point and the CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, 14 months out, parents contributing, wary of 'end-to-end' claims)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
No invented problems; no hard turn-offs found; deferred business details not treated as must-fix

assumptions: Assumed the couple is choosing a ring stone while early in wedding research, consistent with being 14 months out.
